title: Pager Afterlight Notebook - Juno
content:
Quick notes + action items from tonight's pager run. Not formal postmortem — jotting while it's fresh. Mostly fragmented, todo-first style.

Timeline (local timestamps):
- 02:12 — Pager fired: multiple 5xxs for hosted-api /v1/generate (region: us-west1). Alert: 5xx rate > 8% for 90s (INC-4721).
- 02:13 — Confirmed spike on alert dashboard: requests concentrated on model a100-xl-v2, sequence length ~1k. Errors: downstream grpc timeouts to runtime (runt-5).
- 02:16 — Tried quick mitigation: scaled up pool a100-pool-2 by +2 nodes (autoscaler override). k8s commands used: kubectl scale deploy/a100-pool-2 --replicas=6 -n inference.
- 02:19 — After scale, traffic redistributed, 5xx rate dropped to ~1.2%.
- 02:25 — Root cause hypothesis: sudden traffic burst with long sequences exhausted KV cache slots, causing runtime OOM-ish failures and grpc timeouts. Not a pure OOM (no OOMKilled pods), more 'queue overflow' and long GC stalls observed in runt-5 logs.

Immediate follow-ups (do these before EOD):
- [ ] Capture full runt-5 log bundle and upload to /shared/sre/incidents/INC-4721 (assign: Juno) — include thread dumps, kernel messages, and gcore if possible.
- [ ] Create reproducible load script to simulate long-seq bursts against a100-pool-2 (assign: Kai). Use seq lengths 512, 1k, 2k; include KV-cache priming and cold-cache runs. Target: reproduce 5xx within 30 minutes.
- [ ] Update autoscaler policy to allow faster scale for a100-pool-2 when 95p latency > 800ms for 30s (assign: Nisha). Add temporary override window for next 48h.
- [ ] Add alert annotation mapping from INC-4721 to SRE-814 for tracking (assign: Juno).

Runbook gaps observed (candidates for edits):
- No clear step for rapid KV cache warmup as separate mitigation. Add a 'prefill' procedure: run 50 warmup requests to popular prefixes via internal warmup endpoint.
- Autoscaler thresholds for long-sequence workloads are tuned to token throughput, not sequence-length skew. Add guidance: if mean sequence length > 400 for 3m, treat as separate signal.
- Missing example kubectl commands for safe scale overrides (include exact command & rollback note).

Immediate notes for oncall handoff:
- Primary contact for runtime team: @nisha (Slack) / cell on call list.
- If spike reappears after scale, route traffic to fallback model family m-latency-1 (redwood routing policy: route-policy: latency-preference -> fallback).
- Communication: draft short customer note if SLA-sensitive customers hit errors. Notify CS via #cs-incident-ops with tags: INC-4721, high-latency.

Observations (raw):
- runt-5 logs show long pauses in GC + frequent mutex contention around kv-cache map.
- No kernel OOM logs. Pod memory stable ~78% prior to errors, then spike in /proc/vmstat pagefaults.
- Traffic origin: mixture of hostedAPI keys, but one heavy key accounts for ~42% of requests in the 5-minute window. Key id hashed: xxxxx... (opened a privacy ticket).

Commands & snippets I ran (save these, less polished):
- kubectl -n inference logs deploy/runt-5 --since=15m | grep -E "ERROR|panic|timeout" > /tmp/runt5-errors.txt
- nc -vz runtime-host:50051  # sanity tcp check
- curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"a100-xl-v2","input":"<warmup>"}' $HOST/v1/generate | jq '.status'

Notes for postmortem (if we go that route):
- Data to collect: full access logs for 02:00-02:45, runtime metrics (mutex wait times, GC pause), pod-level profiling.
- Hypotheses to test: 1) long-seq driven KV cache exhaustion -> request queuing/timeouts; 2) regression in runt-5 GC settings after last runtime bump (see PR #1987).
- Suggested owners: investigation lead (Juno), telemetry (Kai), runtime fix (Nisha), comms (product ops).

Small personal TODOs (oncall housekeeping):
- [ ] Create follow-up Slack thread summarizing tonight (Juno)
- [ ] Schedule 30m sync with runtime team tomorrow 10:30am PT (Juno + Nisha + Kai)
- [ ] Add a short troubleshooting checklist to runbook: 'check kv-cache metrics -> check mutex wait -> scale pool' (Juno)
- Coffee: refill flask before handoff.

Random scribbles (may be useful):
- If we can detect sequence-length skew early in the gateway, we could route long sequences to a separate pool sized for throughput (cost trade-off).
- Consider adding a cheap per-request token-cost guard to upstream to prevent single key from spiking resource usage for short windows (quota burst smoothing).

End of notes. Leaving midnight handoff at 03:05. Handing over to morning oncall: @kai.
